To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the H2 rotational line fluxes of the western ridge of the IC 443 SNR are very strong, and can be explained by the interaction between the supernova blast wave and ambient molecular clouds.

we have observed the H2 rotational line spectrum in a supernova remnant for the first time and have shown that the H2 emission is consistent with the shock interaction of the supernova blast wave and ambient molecular gas.

we report on the discovery of the first H2 pure rotational line spectra from a supernova remnant, and on the discovery of an H2 shock model that is able to account for all of the H2 pure rotational lines in IC 443.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What is the nature of the interstellar medium in the Milky Way? What are the physical processes that drive the dynamics of the Milky Way? And how do we observe and interpret the data that are collected?
the study of the interaction between the supernova rem- nant IC 443 and its environment.
the study of the interaction between the supernova rem- nant and the surrounding molecular cloud.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the H2 rotational line fluxes observed in IC 443 require shock velocities of 30 to 40kms 1, and that the shock has been propagating in the molecular gas for about 1,000 to 2,000years.
the ISOCAM CVF data are well reproduced by a time-dependent shock model with a shock velocity in the range 20 to 30 km s 1 and a shock age in the range 1000 to 2000 years.
the ISO data are consistent with a shock velocity between 30 and 50kms 1, an age of the remnant of 1,000 to 3,000 years and a pre-shoc density of 10 to 10 4cm 3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have observed a supernova remnant in the phase where the shock has just started to interact with the ambient molecular gas.
the H2 rotational line emission in IC 443 is well reproduced by a shock velocity of about 30kms1 and an age of 1,000 to 2,000 yr.
the observed H2 line fluxes are consistent with a model in which the molecular gas has been heated by a blast wave propagating into a molecular cloud.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ISO data are in agreement with a shock age of about 2,000 yr, which is much younger than the age estimated from the radio observations of IC 443 (about 10,000 yr).
the H2 rotational line emission is an efficient probe of the shock conditions in supernova remnant/molecular gas interactions.

the ISO data provide a direct confirmation of shock models of the H2 emission in the western ridge of IC 443, and that the ISO data are consistent with the hypothesis that this emission is produced in a shock front propagating through a dense cloud of molecular hydrogen.
